findings.title: Grant shortcut matcher uses the wrong offset and inverted comparison
findings.body: The encoded grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 of the six-character prefix, but this matcher reads substring(3, 5) and returns false when it equals the expected shortcut. Consequently, IDs with an incorrect or unknown grant (for example onrtna instead of onrtac) pass the authorization-code assertion as long as the suffix looks like a UUID. Validate the prefix length and reject when substring(4, 6) does not equal the expected shortcut.

findings.title: Shortcut contract recommends a length the decoder cannot support
findings.body: The new getShortcut() contract recommends a three-letter shortcut, whereas DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider requires an exactly six-character context consisting of three two-character shortcuts. A custom grant following this documented contract will issue IDs with a seven-character prefix that the default decoder always rejects. Document the mandatory two-character length and validate it when registering grant shortcuts so invalid providers cannot issue undecodable IDs.
